step1.title: Who is in charge?
step1.ask: Name the lead and the colleagues from each function.
step1.why: An 8D is not done alone: production applies the containment, engineering updates the documents.
step1.how: You = champion. Add at least production and engineering.

step2.title: What is the problem?
step2.ask: Check the customer’s finding — you do not rewrite it.
step2.why: The whole team starts from the same defect, lot and customer.
step2.how: If something is wrong, fix it on the claim sheet, not here.

step3.title: Protect the customer now
step3.ask: Block, isolate, sort, inform — then verify.
step3.why: Bad parts are stopped before looking for the cause (D4).
step3.how: Open the containment tool. Update the status of each action. The sort needs a quantity.

step4.title: Find the real cause
step4.ask: Ishikawa → Pareto → 5 Why, then admin validation.
step4.why: Without a root cause, CAPA actions are just patches.
step4.how: Ishikawa: which families of causes. Pareto: where it happens most. 5 Why: why it appears AND why it was not caught.

step5.title: Correct and prove
step5.ask: Create the CAPA, complete each action, attach a proof.
step5.why: An action without proof is not considered done.
step5.how: The machine action can be yours. The control plan can go to Engineering.

step6.title: Check that it holds
step6.ask: Inspect the following lots: 0 defects of the same type.
step6.why: If the defect comes back, the CAPA is not right: go back to D5.
step6.how: Example: 3 lots after the adjustment, 0 bad parts → you validate.

step7.title: Prevent it elsewhere
step7.ask: Extend the adjustment / inspection to similar workstations.
step7.why: Otherwise the same defect reappears tomorrow on the next workstation.
step7.how: Same machine, same operation → same standard. Tick once it is documented.

step8.title: Close and send to the customer
step8.ask: Internal note, customer PDF, then submit to the admin.
step8.why: The PDF is the document that can be sent to the customer (e.g. Stellantis).
step8.how: Generate the PDF here, review it, then submit. The admin closes it.

s0.title: Start the analysis
s0.what: Open the claim and click “Start analysis”. Enter the line (e.g. crimping station 3) and the production team.
s0.why: Without it, Ishikawa, Pareto, 5 Why and the 8D file stay locked.

s1.title: Who handles the file?
s1.what: In the 8D file, write who leads and who helps.
s1.why: An 8D file is never done alone: it needs an owner and colleagues from each function.
s1.extra1Text: You fill in the 8D, follow up the actions and submit to the admin. Put your name in “8D champion”.
s1.extra2Text: The person on the line (operator or team leader) who saw the defect and can apply the containment / adjustment.
s1.extra3Text: The person who updates the work instructions and the control plan (working documents).

s2.title: What is the problem?
s2.what: Nothing to recreate: it is already the claim sheet (customer, defect type, lot, description).
s2.why: Everyone starts from the same finding: the customer’s.

s3.title: Stop the defect right away (containment management)
s3.what: In D3, run a real immediate action plan: stop shipments, quarantine the lot, sort 100%, inform the customer, check goods in transit. Each action has an owner and a status. The sort requires the quantity checked. Only then tick “containment verified”.
s3.why: The customer is protected before looking for the root cause. A free comment is not enough: it is action management.
s3.extra2Text: Lots in transit, or any other action you add.

s4.title: Find the real cause
s4.what: Use the 3 tools in this order: Ishikawa (which families of causes), Pareto (where it happens most), 5 Why (why it appears AND why it was not detected).
s4.why: Without a root cause, CAPA actions are just patches.

s5.title: Correct and prove
s5.what: From the 5 Why, create the CAPA plan. Take the technical action (e.g. recalibrate the machine). Attach a photo or a report, then “Mark as done”. The documentation action (control plan) can be assigned to Engineering.
s5.why: An action without proof is not considered done.

s6.title: Check that it really worked
s6.what: After the fix, do not close right away. Take the next 3 lots made on the same line. Count the defects of the same type.
s6.why: If these 3 lots have 0 defects, the fix holds. If defects remain, the CAPA is not right: go back to D5.
s6.example: Example: lot A, lot B, lot C produced after adjusting station 3 → 0 bad parts → you tick “effectiveness validated”.

s7.title: Prevent it elsewhere
s7.what: You fixed one station. If other stations do the same work (same machine, same operation), apply the new adjustment or inspection there too.
s7.why: Otherwise the same defect may reappear tomorrow on the next station.
s7.example: Example: the control plan was updated for crimping station 3. Copy it to stations 2 and 4 if they crimp the same way.

s8.title: Close and send to the customer
s8.what: Write the closing note, generate the PDF in its panel (preview + download), then “Submit the file”. The admin validates. The claim becomes closed.
s8.why: The 8D PDF is the document that can be sent to the customer (e.g. Stellantis). It has its own area in D8; it is not a text field.
